data.name: Sargent
data.long_meaning: From the Old French 'serjant', derived from 'serviens' meaning 'servant' or 'attendant'. The name Sargent came to signify a military rank, as a leader or commander of a group.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes leadership, courage, and service in one's community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sargent has historical roots in the military sphere, specifically as a term for an officer or a leader, as well as being the English title of a painter, John Singer Sargent. It carries a sense of achievement, discipline, and responsibility, and continues to be a common name in the English-speaking world.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian context, the name Sargent can be viewed as a reminder of the calling to serve God and others selflessly. In Matthew 20:26-27, Jesus teaches that true greatness lies not in worldly power, but in serving and caring for others. Sargent, meaning 'servant,' echoes this biblical theme and offers an opportunity to reflect on the importance of humility and service in both our personal and professional lives.
